- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.5), model underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to align with mean-reversion bias.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, reduce forecast by 5–10% in the next 3–5 periods to correct for momentum decay.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days moving toward historical mean), model often lags; adjust forecast to align with 3-period moving average of true values.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates in early periods (1–5 days) after sentiment shift; apply downward bias of 3–7% for first 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5–7 days to calibrate forecast.
